record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: Let G be the direct product of k≥2 copies of SL(2,R), let U+ and U− be the upper and lower unipotent subgroups, and let Γ+ and Γ− be irreducible lattices in U+ and U−. If the group generated by Γ+ and Γ− is discrete, is it an arithmetic lattice in G?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 34 (G. Margulis, A. Selberg). If the group 〈Γ+ , Γ− 〉is discrete, then it is an arithmetic lattice in G.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k \geq 2$ be an integer and let $G = \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})^k$. Let 
$$U^+ = \left\{\begin{pmatrix} 1 & * \\ 0 & 1 \end{pmatrix}\right\}^k \subset G, \qquad U^- = \left\{\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ * & 1 \end{pmatrix}\right\}^k \subset G$$
be the subgroups of upper-triangular and lower-triangular unipotent elements, both isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^k$. A lattice $\Lambda$ in $U^\pm \cong \mathbb{R}^k$ is called irreducible if it is not contained in any proper sum of coordinate subspaces (equivalently, no finite-index subgroup of $\Lambda$ splits as a product of lattices in coordinate subgroups). Let $\Gamma^+$ be an irreducible lattice in $U^+$ and $\Gamma^-$ an irreducible lattice in $U^-$.

Assume that the subgroup $\langle \Gamma^+, \Gamma^- \rangle$ of $G$ generated by $\Gamma^+ \cup \Gamma^-$ is discrete. Prove or disprove: $\langle \Gamma^+, \Gamma^- \rangle$ is an arithmetic lattice in $G$.
artifact.category_tag: Arithmeticity of lattices in Lie groups
artifact.status_search_result: A theorem of Benoist and Miquel ("Arithmeticity of discrete subgroups containing horospherical lattices", Duke Math. J. 2020) establishes that in a semisimple real algebraic Lie group of real rank at least 2, any discrete Zariski-dense subgroup containing an irreducible lattice of a horospherical (unipotent) subgroup is an arithmetic lattice. This includes the case $G = \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})^k$ with $k \geq 2$ and resolves the Margulis–Selberg conjecture in the stated form.

status_evidence.title: Arithmeticity of discrete subgroups containing horospherical lattices
status_evidence.snippet: A discrete Zariski-dense subgroup of G that contains an irreducible lattice of U is an arithmetic lattice of G, which solves a conjecture of Margulis and extends previous works of Selberg and Oh.
status_evidence.claim: Benoist–Miquel prove that any discrete Zariski-dense subgroup of a higher-rank semisimple Lie group containing an irreducible lattice of a horospherical subgroup is arithmetic, solving Margulis's conjecture; this covers G = SL(2,R)^k with k ≥ 2.

status_evidence.title: Arithmeticity of discrete subgroups (Benoist lecture notes)
status_evidence.snippet: In the mid 90's, G. Margulis raised a conjecture... if Γ is a discrete Zariski dense subgroup of G that contains an irreducible lattice of U, then Γ is a non-cocompact irreducible arithmetic lattice of G.
status_evidence.claim: States the Margulis conjecture in the horospherical-lattice form and surveys its resolution.
